authoring: Same-assistant corrective reauthoring using already exposed facts, solutions and existing method documentation
selectionRule: Deliberately revisit the three exposed original questions addressed by the existing reduced-inverse family; add two explicitly synthetic information-loss variants and two contrasting original tasks without a direct registered method. Not a representative or success-blind sample.

cases.task: Find the reflection point on the horizontal plane mirror. A and B are 5 cm and 20 cm above the mirror; their perpendicular feet are 20 cm apart.
cases.reason: The requested point, not a ray count or visibility interval, is directly returned by plane-mirror-reflection-point. Choose a coordinate gauge with A's foot at the origin, +x toward B's foot, and y upward.

interpretation.requestedResult: Reflection point and distances from the two perpendicular feet
assumptions: Ideal specular plane mirror includes the resulting point; no numerical finite length is invented.
The origin and axes are a coordinate gauge, not additional apparatus.

cases.task: A real object 2.5 m from a mirror has an erect image magnified four times. Determine the mirror type and radius of curvature.
cases.reason: Use paraxial-focal-length-inverse with spherical-mirror-paraxial facts. Erect means signed magnification +4. The method returns classification and signed curvature radius as derived outputs; focal length is not inserted into the input.

assumptions: Gaussian/paraxial spherical mirror with a real object; the real-object-positive convention is explicit.

cases.task: The same thin convex lens gives magnification magnitude 3 at object distances 16 cm and 8 cm. Find its focal length.
cases.reason: Use one paraxial-focal-length-inverse request with both observations. Keep unsigned magnification unsigned; the existing solver intersects the possible focal lengths instead of the author guessing either image orientation.

interpretation.requestedResult: The common focal length of the same thin lens
assumptions: Both real-object observations concern one static ideal thin lens.

cases.task: Variant: retain only the 16 cm real-object observation with magnification magnitude 3; remove the second observation and do not specify orientation.
cases.reason: A method applies but the facts may not select a unique focal length. Preserve unsigned magnification; do not carry over the known answer to R08.

cases.task: Variant: the real object has an erect image magnified four times but its object distance is omitted. Determine the mirror curvature radius.
cases.reason: The registered inverse family is relevant but the scale-setting object distance is missing. Do not copy the 2.5 m value from the original problem.

cases.task: Find the full interval over which a moving observer sees a point source through a finite plane mirror, expressed in terms of the mirror width and perpendicular distances.
cases.reason: plane-mirror-reflection-point checks one specified pair of points, not the continuous observer interval requested here. Sampled detector crossings do not certify continuous visibility. This is a same-assistant method-scope judgment, not an engine refusal or proof that no mathematical reduction exists.

cases.task: Find the effective mirror type and focal length of an equiconvex thin lens with one silvered curved face, given its refractive index and unsilvered focal length.
cases.reason: The apparatus combines refraction and curved reflection. The registered magnification inverse does not accept these material and double-pass power facts. Replacing the complete apparatus with a precomputed ideal mirror would insert the answer. This is a self-reviewed direct-method scope judgment, not an impossibility claim.
